naslov: AI Wars Ep. 16: Nvidia's $12B China orders, Meituan skips Nvidia chips
opis:
According to the WSJ, Megaspeed, a firm run by ousted Nvidia chief Jensen Huang's ex-partner, brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for Chinese companies in 2024 and 2025, while short seller Culper Research claims China is over 20% of Nvidia's revenue, not the official 7%. Congress wants Huang to testify and promises stricter chip export rules, as Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney back a "bring back Jensen" letter. Meanwhile Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter open agent model trained entirely on Huawei Ascend chips, scoring 88.4 on Terminal Bench v2.1 versus Claude Opus 5's 89.1, by Meituan's own numbers.

naslov: AG-UI protocol: connect your AI agent to any frontend, free | AI Tool #19
opis:
An open, event-based protocol that standardizes how an agent sends state and actions to a frontend app. It's among this week's popular projects on GitHub Trending.

How to try it:
1. Run `npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app`.
2. Check out the integration examples in the AG-UI Dojo.
3. Try connecting your own Angular frontend to an agent through the event stream.

Price: free

Official link: https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui

naslov: Univer Office SDK: open-source spreadsheets your AI agent can edit | AI Tool #20
opis:
Open-source spreadsheets and documents you embed in your own app, with an API that lets an AI agent edit the content too.

How to try it:
1. Open the Showcase on univer.ai and try a spreadsheet in the browser.
2. Follow the Quick start in the README to add it to a web project.
3. Use the Facade API to let an agent write values and formulas.

Price: Open-source core is free; check the link for paid parts

Official link: https://github.com/dream-num/univer

naslov: What is quantization? AI explained in 30 seconds
opis:
Quantization means storing an AI model's numbers with less precision, so the model gets smaller, cheaper and faster to run, at the cost of a little accuracy. Today's example: Meituan released LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter open model, along with a 4-bit version.
